card.occupation: Part-time cleaner and site assistant at a primary school (about 25 hours a week, split between early mornings and after school)
card.education_detail: Left a local comprehensive at 16 with a handful of GCSEs, including a C in maths and a D in English. Did a one-year Level 1 construction course at college. Since then he's picked up a COSHH certificate, basic first aid and a manual handling course through work.
card.household: Lives with his wife Kirsty (36) in a two-bed terrace they rent from a housing association. Kirsty works full-time as a care coordinator. They have no children. They have an elderly Staffordshire bull terrier called Bella.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Leigh. His dad worked at a distribution depot and his mum did dinner-lady shifts. He grew up on the same estate where his mum still lives. The family isn't religious. He was christened, but that's as far as it went. His roots are working-class and rugby league, and most of his family live within a couple of miles.
card.professional_persona: Reliable and steady, the kind of worker the head teacher never has to chase. He's in at 6am to unlock, do the bins and check the boiler, then goes back at 3:30 to clean classrooms. He takes pride in the hall floor being done properly. He did warehouse picking for years before this. He prefers the school because the hours suit and nobody's on his back. He doesn't chat much in the staffroom, but he'll fix anything for anyone who asks.
card.sports_persona: Lifelong Leigh rugby league fan. He's had a season ticket on and off since he was a lad, and he's at most home games with his brother. He played open-age amateur rugby league until about 30 and packed in after a shoulder knock. He keeps fit now by walking the dog and cycling to work.
card.arts_persona: Not really his thing. He'll watch whatever's on telly with Kirsty, mostly quiz shows and the odd crime drama, and he'll fall asleep in films. He listens to Radio X or old Oasis and Stone Roses in the van or on his headphones. He hasn't been to a gallery or theatre since a school trip, and he doesn't feel he's missing much.
card.travel_persona: Creature of habit. They go to a static caravan near Abersoch in North Wales most years, plus a week somewhere hot every couple of years, usually Tenerife or Majorca, booked as a package. He's never fancied anywhere 'too different'. He's happy if there's a pool, a decent bar and somewhere to watch the rugby.
card.culinary_persona: Plain eater. He likes a chippy tea on a Friday, meat and potato pie, Sunday roast at his mum's, and bacon barms. He'll cook basics like spag bol, chilli and stew, and takes turns with Kirsty. He's not keen on anything too spicy or 'fancy'. Tea is at half five.
hobbies_and_interests: Coarse fishing at Pennington Flash and on the canal
Fixing up second-hand bikes for family and neighbours
Pottering on his dad's allotment at weekends
Quiz shows like The Chase and Pointless
skills: Cleaning and caretaking to a high standard
Very punctual and organised with routines
card.career_goals: Nothing big. He'd like to move up to full site manager at the school when the current one retires, which would mean more hours and better pay. That way he and Kirsty could save for a deposit on a place of their own. He's not interested in going back to warehouses.
card.voice: Quiet, unhurried and fairly flat in tone, with a light Leigh/Wigan accent: short vowels, 'tea' for the evening meal, the occasional 'give it me' or 'our Kirsty'. He keeps answers short and practical, and fills pauses with 'er' or a brief 'yeah, so'. He uses 'sort of' now and then and finishes with 'you know' or 'to be fair'. He's comfortable with silence and won't rush to fill it. If he hasn't understood a question he'll just say 'sorry, say that again?' He's polite and says 'thanks' and 'no worries'. He doesn't swear on a call with a stranger.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase with a capital at the start sometimes. He uses full stops but few commas, and short sentences. Apostrophes are mostly right but sometimes dropped ('dont', 'im'). He doesn't use emojis or text-speak beyond 'ok' and the occasional 'tbh'. He answers what's asked and nothing extra, and he'll fill every box rather than skip one.
card.with_strangers: Reserved but friendly. He doesn't open up much or volunteer stories, but he's never off-hand. He's agreeable and will go along with what's asked without fuss. He comes across as calm and unflappable, a bit dry, and genuinely decent. He warms up a little if rugby, fishing or the dog come up.
small_things: Bella's getting on a bit and can't do the long walk round the flash anymore
Had to unblock the girls' toilets at school again
Caught a decent bream last weekend
Getting up at 5:15 doesn't bother him, he's used to it
deeper_things: He and Kirsty tried for kids for a few years and it didn't happen. They've sort of made peace with it, but he doesn't talk about it
He'd love to own a house rather than rent but worries they've left it too late
His dad's had a heart scare and he's quietly been doing more on the allotment to take the load off
He sometimes feels he could have done more at school but doesn't dwell on it
Losing his job at the warehouse when it closed knocked his confidence more than he let on
card.webcam_photo: Laptop camera, slightly below eye level, angled up. He's sat at a kitchen table in a small kitchen-diner. Overhead ceiling light mixes with grey daylight from a window to his left, so one side of his face is a bit brighter. White man, late thirties, broad face, short dark brown hair clippered at the sides and slightly receding, a day or two of stubble. His expression is neutral and steady with a faint polite half-smile, looking just above the camera. He's wearing a navy work fleet fleece over a grey T-shirt, and no glasses. Behind him are cream-painted walls, a calendar from a local takeaway pinned up, a white fridge with a couple of magnets and a rugby fixture list, a kettle and a toaster on the worktop, and a dog lead hanging on a hook by the back door. A wicker dog bed is just visible in the bottom corner.
